title: Occasional crashes in nightlies when unlocking laptop
body:
### What Operating System(s) are you seeing this problem on?

macOS

### Which Wayland compositor or X11 Window manager(s) are you using?

_No response_

### WezTerm version

20230108-184945-d34297cd

### Did you try the latest nightly build to see if the issue is better (or worse!) than your current version?

Yes, and I updated the version box above to show the version of the nightly that I tried

### Describe the bug

The nightlies for the last few weeks have been occasionally crashing for me. Usually it happens shortly after unlocking my MacBook. I'll wake up the machine, unlock it, and WezTerm will disappear shortly after the desktop is displayed. Sometimes it has already crashed by the time the desktop becomes visible.

This has been happening for many nightly versions for the past few weeks (I've been updating every day or two). The crashes aren't frequent, maybe once every two or three days. WezTerm hasn't crashed when I've been actively using the machine (thankfully 🙂).

I'm not 100% sure when the crashes started happening, but based on the last app crash log (which is the first one I've taken the time to look at), it seems like the crash may be related to the new menu bar. I've included that below in case it's useful.

This report is quite vague, but I thought it was worth reporting in case there was some low hanging fruit in the menu generating code.

### To Reproduce

I don't have any good reproduction instructions since the issue happens very sporadically.

### Configuration

no config

### Expected Behavior

_No response_

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
Hmm, sounds like it is related to the new macOS menubar stuff.
The trace above isn't super accurate, so it's difficult to dive in as is; do you think you could build from source and run a version with debug symbols?

Follow the steps with the full git repo from:
https://wezfurlong.org/wezterm/install/source.html

but before you run the build, uncomment this line:
https://github.com/participant1/wezterm/blob/c65db44d3e7eee67098a57c97b7c02dadd95fd09/Cargo.toml#L20

then continue with:

```
cargo build --release
./ci/deploy.sh
```

that will build you a WezTerm.app bundle that has full debug symbols.

If you could run that for a few days and report back with any crash report that is generated, that would be helpful!

Please also share:
* Which version of macOS you are running
* Do you have multiple wezterm windows open at the time of the fault
* If you have any utilities installed that might inject bundles and/or influence other apps. I'm thinking of hotkey/shortcut/menu utilities from third parties.

comments.author: participant1
comments.body: re: macOS version, I can see from what you already shared that it is `macOS 13.1 (22C65)`.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
I'll give that a shot.

From the trace it looked like the problem was happening in Menu::items in `window/src/os/macos/menu.rs`, presumably in the `msg_send!` macro. Maybe the menu pointer became invalid at some point?

I generally do have 2 or 3 WezTerm windows open at a time, each with a few tabs, and most tabs will have at least split. I do not run any utilities (that I'm aware of) that should be injecting code into running apps.

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
Yeah, it's likely in there, but sometimes those traces are wildly off when there's no debug info, so it's good to make sure.

The number/nature of windows is potentially significant, as the system will manipulate the contents of the window menu in certain circumstances to update the windows shown there.

FWIW, I've been running the same build for a couple of weeks and haven't had this issue, but I generally only have 1 window open.

I'll open a spare one to see if I can persuade it to happen for me.

comments.body:
Seems inconclusive.  If you have developer tools installed, running `lldb -p $(pgrep wezterm-gui)` to launch the debugger, and then running `bt all` will get the best fidelity information about what wezterm is up to.

@reporter another option for you to capture info is to attach lldb (do that from Terminal.app) and leave it attached until something goes wrong.  You'll want to type `continue` at the prompt to let it continue running after you attach.  If/when it goes wrong, it should hang rather than vanish and you can capture a stack trace by running `bt all`.

Interesting insight! Appearance changes trigger a config reload, which in turn may rebuild/adjust the menubar contents.

I think I've found a pretty good repro: triple press CMD-R which reloads the config three times in quick succession. That gets me a similar stack trace and something to work from.

comments.author: participant1
comments.body: I think I found it; I pushed a commit that makes my repro no longer cause a crash

comments.author: reporter
comments.body: Interesting. For me it consistently (so far 100% of the time) happens if I press CMD-R 5 times. It can be 5 times in a row, or with various delays, or even with other things happening between the config reloads. Like, I can press CMD-R 4 times, type into the terminal, create and remove splits, and focus other windows, and when I refocus WT and press CMD-R for the 5th time WT will crash. It's extremely consistent.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body: Weird that the 5 count is so consistent for me. Maybe it's a fluke, or something related to my local build?

comments.author: reporter
comments.body: That update appears to resolve the issue for me, as well. At least, repeatedly reloading the config doesn't crash WT. 🙂

comments.author: participant1
comments.body: The bug I fixed was a refcounting problem where we'd think we owned a reference to the main menu and would release it when we're done referencing it. If its internal reference count was normally say 4 then on the 5th reload NSApp would return a stale/freed menu bar and problems would ensue.  For me it triggered after pressing at least 3 times. I may have pressed more than 3; I just spammed it until the stack trace showed up in lldb.

comments.author: participant1
comments.body: Fingers crossed that this fixes the other stack traces as well: I feel reasonably confident about it(!)
